resources.string: Using apps in the background needs two things: accessibility (so X Assistant can see and tap) and a one-time “Wireless debugging” pairing (so it can open apps on a background screen). Accessibility alone cannot create that screen, so Developer options stay required. Everything happens on the phone, with no computer. The first time takes about 10 minutes. Web, files and chat work without this.
You can skip this for now and just use web, files and chat; X Assistant will remind you the first time it needs an app.
Open “About phone” in Settings and tap “Build number” 7 times until you see “You are now a developer”. On some phones “Build number” is under “Software information”.
In “Developer options”, find “USB debugging”, turn it on and tap “OK” when asked. No cable needed: with it on, X Assistant can keep working even when Wi-Fi is off.

Find X Assistant in “Accessibility” and turn it on. Then it reads the pairing code itself, so you don’t type it. If the switch is grey or Android says “restricted setting”, allow that in App info first, then come back. You can skip this and type the code from the notification instead.
X Assistant reads the pairing code itself

In “Developer options”, find “Wireless debugging” and turn it on. When asked, choose “Allow” and tick “Always allow on this network” so you won’t be asked again. You need to be on Wi-Fi (internet access not required).
Just be on Wi-Fi; no internet needed
Open “Wireless debugging”, then tap “Pair device with pairing code”. A 6-digit code appears on screen.
Once paired, X Assistant connects and gets ready by itself in a few seconds.
Skip for now and type the code myself
Can’t turn it on? Allow restricted settings in App info first
When the code appears, wait a few seconds — X Assistant reads it and finishes pairing. No need to leave that page.
Tap any step above to go back and redo it.
X Assistant reads “Developer options” as off (some phones report it wrong). Go back and make sure it’s on.
“Wireless debugging” seems to be off: X Assistant reads it as off. Go back and make sure it’s on and you’re on Wi-Fi.
This phone doesn’t let X Assistant read the “Wireless debugging” switch. Go back and make sure it’s on and you’re on Wi-Fi.
Found the pairing window. Enter the code in the notification.
The pairing code goes into a notification, so allow X Assistant’s notifications first.
“Needs you” and “Task results” notifications won’t pop up now, so you may miss when you’re needed. You can continue, or turn them on now.
The pairing window closes when you leave it. Use split screen to see the code and type here at the same time.
The number after the colon in “IP address & port” in the pairing window
Only needed if X Assistant can’t find the pairing window
Pairing and connecting, just a few seconds
Keep USB debugging on. After a restart, turn on Wireless debugging and X Assistant reconnects automatically.
The code changes each time the pairing window opens. Tap “Pair device with pairing code” again and enter the new 6 digits.
Keep the window showing the code open while you enter it. Open it again and retry.
X Assistant needs Wi-Fi to start phone control (no internet needed). It resumes by itself once you join any Wi-Fi.
Wireless debugging isn’t allowed on this Wi-Fi yet

X Assistant turned on Wireless debugging, but the system didn’t allow it on this Wi-Fi. Turn on “Wireless debugging” once yourself; when asked, tick “Always allow on this network” and tap Allow. After that X Assistant can turn it on by itself on this Wi-Fi.
Couldn’t find the Wireless debugging port. You can: turn “Wireless debugging” off and on again, then retry; switch to a phone hotspot or your home Wi-Fi; or enter the port below.
The system may have revoked it after a long time unused, or it was removed. Just pair again. Turn on “Disable adb authorization timeout” in Developer options so it won’t expire again.
Retry first; if that doesn’t work, pair again.
Uses wireless debugging to control apps on a virtual screen

After pairing once, X Assistant’s built-in helper stays in the background and keeps working even without Wi-Fi. Keep “USB debugging” (in Developer options) on; turning it off stops phone control. After a restart, join Wi-Fi and turn on “Wireless debugging” and X Assistant reconnects by itself — no new code needed.
Connected and able to use apps
Connected; stops if Wi-Fi drops unless “USB debugging” is on
Not paired yet; set it up once before using apps
Paired; connects automatically once Wireless debugging is on
No Wi-Fi; resumes once you join any Wi-Fi
Turn on Wireless debugging once yourself and tick “Always allow on this network”
If it won’t connect, or after changing phone settings
Delete the pairing and stop phone control

X Assistant will delete the pairing, stop using apps on the virtual screen, and revoke the permissions granted through the switches below. Web and file tasks aren’t affected. To use apps again later, you’ll need to pair once more. You can also remove X Assistant under “Wireless debugging → Paired devices” in system settings.
Phone control isn’t ready, so X Assistant can’t use apps this time; web and files work as usual.
Type the 6 digits shown on screen here — no need to leave the pairing window
Phone control is set up. You can go back to X Assistant now
Go back to X Assistant to see how to fix it
Wrong or expired code: in the pairing window, tap “Pair device with pairing code” again to get a new code, then enter it again
The pairing window closed or the code expired: tap “Pair device with pairing code” again to get a new code, then enter it again
X Assistant’s notification pops up at the top of the screen; if not, swipe down to open the notification shade
The pairing code goes into a notification, so turn on X Assistant’s “%1$s” notifications first.

X Assistant’s “%1$s” notifications won’t pop up at the top of the screen now. Turn on “Pop on screen” so you can enter the code right over the pairing window; otherwise swipe down to the notification shade to enter it.
Looking for the Wireless debugging port on this phone…
On the “Wireless debugging” page, the number after the colon in “IP address & port”, e.g. 41235
If Android says “restricted setting”: open App info, tap ⋮ at the top right, choose “Allow restricted settings”, then turn accessibility on. That menu sometimes appears only after the first block.

The code expires in about a minute. If it fails or expires, tap “Pair device with pairing code” again for a new 6-digit code. If the notification does not pop up, swipe down the notification shade. Don’t leave the pairing window while you type. If the notification is awkward, enter the code below.
